trigger: Cyber insurance renewal requiring Essential Eight controls

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Aisha Rahman, thanks for making time. I have Port Phillip Physio Group as seventy-six people across St Kilda and Cheltenham, and you run operations as general manager, right?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: That's right. We've physios, reception, admin and a small leadership team. The immediate issue is our cyber insurance renewal, which has become much stricter than last year.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: What is the insurer asking for that you can't easily evidence today?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: They want proof of MFA, patching, backups and admin controls. Our provider says those things are handled, but when I ask for records I get screenshots and a long email rather than a clean answer.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: How does IT support work across the two clinics during a normal week?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Reception logs issues by email, then people chase by phone if it's urgent. Clinicians can't wait long because the practice system, EFTPOS and exercise software all touch appointments.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Who will make the decision if you change support before the renewal?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: I recommend, the clinic director approves, and finance signs the contract. The director cares about patient privacy and not disrupting sessions. Finance cares about predictability.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: What would success look like in the first six weeks?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: An evidence pack for the insurer, a known helpdesk process for reception, a cleaned-up Microsoft 365 tenant, and less noise when staff move between clinics. We're not trying to become a bank, just competent.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Where are staff most likely to resist a change?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Reception will resist if it slows them down. Clinicians will resist if passwords or MFA interrupt appointments. The director will resist anything that sounds like a generic cyber package.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: For your size, Harbourline IT would be around $126 per seat per month, with an onboarding project to produce the Essential Eight evidence and standardise clinic support.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Our current provider says they already do security, so I need to understand why this is different. I do not want to pay twice for the same promise.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: That is fair. The difference should be visible in evidence, ownership and cadence. We would show which controls exist, which are partial and which need work, then report monthly instead of waiting for renewal season. I will send the Essential Eight evidence plan and commercial proposal by Thursday.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: That's a better answer. The clinic director will also ask how you avoid disruption during appointment hours.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I will include the staged clinic rollout and receptionist training plan. We can run identity changes after the final appointment block and do short reception sessions before the morning rush.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Good. The price is workable if the onboarding project is clear and if finance can see what risk is reduced.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Can we meet Thursday 10 September at 3pm with you, the clinic director and finance to review the proposal and evidence plan?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Yes, Thursday 10 September at 3pm works. Send the invite and I will add the other two.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: For the insurer, we will avoid vague maturity claims. The evidence plan will state which Essential Eight controls are in place, which are partly in place, and what dates we can put against improvements.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: That's exactly what I need. Our board doesn't expect perfection, but they do expect a straight answer and a plan they can defend.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: We can also separate clinical-impact changes from back-office changes. Anything that touches appointment flow gets tested in one clinic first, with reception feedback before it goes wider.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: That will matter. Reception knows where the friction really sits, and they will tell us quickly if a new login process is getting in the way.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I will write the proposal so finance can see monthly support, onboarding and optional maturity work as separate lines. That should make the decision less all-or-nothing.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Good. A clear split will help, because I can get urgent insurance work approved faster than broad improvement work.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The receptionist training will be short and role-specific. It should answer where to log issues, what to do if EFTPOS or the practice system is affected, and how to escalate urgent appointment-impacting problems.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: That's practical. Reception carries the stress first, so if they trust the process the clinicians will usually follow.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Will do. I will send the proposal the morning of the meeting so you've time to skim it.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Aisha Rahman
turns.text: Thanks Jordan. This feels more grounded than the last few calls I have had.
